column1: # Lote 04 — narrative.gd (fim das legendas de chegada, legendas de zona limpa, cards do epílogo)

column2: The shrine's Praetorian carries a buckler. Heavy blows, or from behind.
Six Rings turn in my hand as if they knew each other. Parts of a single thing.
They are. They are the key. It lacks only the seventh tooth.
Velkar said there's a child up there. You never told me that.
Because there is none. There is a throne, and the throne is your enemy.
The antechamber of the Crown. After it, the seventh. And then... the rite. I promised to show you.
A crown too tall for the head that wears it. He knows. That's why he shouts.
Good. They return to the ground, and the ground to sleep.
They don't scream. They just lie down... as if they were grateful.
Every spark you free grows lighter. Do you feel it? They rise because of you.
They rise because of me... to where?
Do not stop to think here. In Torpor, thinking turns into dozing.
(A taste of warm milk in my mouth. Where does that come from?)
They fall with open hands. No one clenches a fist to sleep.
The sleep of this Aeon has long fingers. Climb.
Torpor hates no one. It only wants company.
How many of these were once sparks like me?
Do you feel the mist thickening? It is fear. He knows you are coming.
An Archon, afraid of me?
(The stone spoke of a Wisdom who wanted to see the Source alone. Why does that name hurt?)
Devoured by their own teeth. Hunger always ends this way.
They fall with their mouths open. Still hungry.
A fine blow. I would have applauded, if I had hands.
No one here sells anything. They just trade one hunger for another.
Food, sleep, coin: every chain begins soft.
(I'm hungry too. But not for bread.)
Harmas charges for every memory. Buy nothing. Not even longing.
What if I already sold something here without knowing?
The merchants close their stalls when you pass. They know you already.
Or they're afraid of what I carry.
Do not stop. Hunger smells those who stop.
While he was talking, the Voice said nothing. Nothing.
If the Blind One made the seven in his image... what falls when the seven fall?
The seals fall. Their order was only rust.
They cry ‘law’ as they die. None of them says ‘justice’.
Every broken seal is one less chain in the world. You are good at this.
Good at breaking. The Voice never praises me for anything else.
Do not philosophize with the jailer. He loves it.
If fate is a chain, who holds the other end?
The stars will not stop turning for you. Climb.
(The two Rings chime against each other, as if they were talking.)
The links have names carved in them. None is mine. Yet.
Nor will it be. I would not allow it.
Borrowed clay, Bearer. Do not cling to the body: it is only the ladder.
If the clay is his and the breath isn't... what's mine?
I can hear the throne's chains from here. They sing low. It sounds like weeping.
They fall without a sound. Like pages.
One silence fewer. The world already sounds louder.
There's a question I don't ask, because I'm afraid of the answer.
Then do not ask it. Here, a question turns into blank ink.
Gnosis isn't faith or works, says the stone: it's remembering. And I remember nothing before the ashes.
You will remember when the seven Rings are together. I promise.
Silence sticks to your boots. Climb.
(A fallen book. Blank. But my hand knows where every word was.)
Buried books save no one. The one who saves you is me, and I am here.
(Sixteen centuries under the earth, and they still speak.)
Closer. The shelves end soon.
Why do you go quiet when Soter appears?
On the other side of the door, not even the air moves.
When they fall, the shards show a face. Never their own.
Do not look at the shards. Look at the path.
The Voice hates this Aeon more than the others. Why?
Because mirrors lie better than I ever would.
Do I have his strength, or does he have mine?
You have your own. Enough. Climb.
Four Rings. Do you feel how they pull? They are in a hurry.
They pull. But not upward: toward each other.
Do not linger by the water. It gives back more than it shows.
(At the bottom of the puddle, for an instant: a white cloud, and someone small crying in it.)
Valentinus, Basilides... dead men arguing over what they never saw.
They argued about the same thing I do: where I came from, and where I go back to.
Behind the door, someone is breathing in time with me.
They rot before they fall. They had been dead a long time.
The puddle drains away. Good. Do not step in what is left.
How much of me is matter, and how much is breath?
The breath. Only that. The rest is borrowed clay.
The Blight gets in through the feet of those who stop. Climb.
(The living here don't ask for a cure. They ask for it to end soon.)
Does what's inside me save me? And what if what's inside is dark?
Then I am your light. That is enough.
Do not breathe deep here. Not even to sigh.
Five Rings, each warmer than the last. As if they recognized me.
The prince's robe was waiting for him up above. Is something waiting for me?
Ina, Merou, Tasso. I say the names softly, so I won't forget.
Breathe. On the other side, only the Crown and me.
Crowns fall from higher up and make more noise. That is all.
They die calling for the king. None of them knows his name.
Nearly, Bearer. Nearly. I feel all seven one step away.
The Voice has never been in such a hurry. Never.
If salvation is a return... where do I return to?
To me. To where it all began.
Do not stop. Not even to read. You know enough already.
(I know enough to be suspicious. Not enough to stop.)
The air here smells of old gold and fear. Climb.
Velkar talks too much for one who lost everything. Do not carry his words.
The stones say the body is only an appearance. Then why does it hurt so much?
Save the spark, Bearer. The body is for climbing.
(The stones say one thing; the Voice, another. One of them is wrong. Or both.)
The seven spheres went out like oil lamps at dawn. The Archons became again what they had always been: names.
Those who slept did not wake. They simply stopped dreaming. No one asked if they wanted to.
In the lap of the Source, a child learned to see. The mother looked back once. Enough to remember; not to stay.
The crown weighed less than he had said. That should have been the warning.
Seven thrones, seven new husks. The Kenoma did not notice the difference. She looked after everyone. Everyone.
So many times she had tasted their gifts. The throne only felt familiar.
One day, in a city of ash, someone woke and heard a gentle voice: “Wake. The ashes beneath your feet were your people.”
She went down from door to door, knocking at the houses of those who sleep. Some opened. Others asked for a little more dream. She waited.
In the city of ash she learned the names. Ina, who sang off-key. Merou, of the well. Tasso, of the roof. She said each one aloud.
They were not her people. Now they are. And inside her, small, someone was learning to see.
The spark remembered. The rest is silence.
